body:
When you’re a kid, fun comes first. Final exams, driver’s ed, and summer jobs will arrive soon enough. Cub Scouts helps kids (whatever their gender) have fun while teaching them skills that will help them later in life. From the thrill of practicing archery to learning how to transform a block of wood into a race car, Cub Scouts is one thrill after another. With a program expertly tailored to match each age in a young person's life, Cub Scouts learn that even when fun isn’t easy, it’s always an adventure. In Scouting, everything has a purpose, and it shows kids that doing their best is the most fun of all. Pack 120 was originally chartered with the Keezletown Ruritans in Keezletown, Virginia, for many years we were hosted by Vision of Hope UMC on Port Republic Road in Rockingham, Virginia. As of 2024, we are delighted to be hosted by Massanutten Presbyterian Church. We welcome any Scout, but we currently draw primarily from Cub Run and Peak View Elementary Schools in Rockingham County, with several scouts also coming from elementary schools in Harrisonburg.
As one of the largest and most active Cub Scout Packs in the Mountain Valley District of the Virginia Headwaters Council, our vibrant group of kids and involved parents plan numerous events throughout the year, service-oriented projects, along with fun and educational trips within the Shenandoah Valley and surrounding areas.
We typically hold our Pack meetings on the second or third Monday of each month at 6:00 pm at Massanutten Presbyterian Church (50 Indian Trail Rd, Penn Laird, VA 22846). Our Scouts enjoy the outdoors, so we hold as many outdoor activities as we can.
One of the primary goals of Pack 120 is to ensure the Scouts have a positive Scouting experience, receive every opportunity to participate in events, and enjoy the journey. Scouting is what the Scouts and families make of the program, and we continue to have a great group of Scouts and parents making this happen every year.
title: About Pack 120

body:
In Cubscouts, all of the cubs in an area are members of a Pack (ours is Pack 120). The Pack has several smaller units, usually at least one per grade in elementary school, called Dens.
Michael Stewart I'm so happy to finally get to return to scouting! I was in scouts in my youth and earned the Eagle Scout rank. I benefitted from the hard work of so many leaders and mentors, and am delighted to pay it forward. My daughter Mary's crossed over to Troop 242 and my son Charlie is in the Bear den this year. Outside of scouting, I am a professor in the Department of Computer Science at JMU. I enjoy cooking, eating, playing games, learning, hiking, and hearing about your pets.
Cubmaster Pack Asst. Den Leader Den 8 Bear Missy Luikart I'm so glad to be able to participate in Scouting America! I watched my brother learn so much in scouts and wanted to go where he went and learn what he learned. I've always loved the outdoors, and I'm so happy to lead a den of sweet girls, including my daughter, and help Michael as Assistant Cubmaster. I also have a son in Troop 40, and a younger son not quite ready for Cub Scouts yet. Welcome to our Pack!
Assistant Cubmaster Pack Den Leader Den 7 Webelos Jeremy Akers I'm a proud dad with one son in Troop 40 and another in the Wolf den. As a professor of nutrition at James Madison University, I’m passionate about education and growth; both in the classroom and in the outdoors. I love hiking, fishing, and hunting, and I truly enjoy watching Scouts grow, learn, and thrive through the adventures and values of the pack. Welcome to Pack 120!

body:
Cuando eres niño, la diversión es lo primero. Los exámenes finales, la clase de manejo y los trabajos de verano llegarán pronto. Los Cub Scouts ayudan a los niños (sin importar su género) a divertirse mientras les enseñan habilidades que les serán útiles más adelante. Desde la emoción de practicar tiro con arco hasta aprender a transformar un bloque de madera en un auto de carreras, los Cub Scouts son una experiencia tras otra. Con un programa diseñado por expertos para cada edad, los Cub Scouts aprenden que, aunque la diversión no sea fácil, siempre es una aventura. En el Escultismo, todo tiene un propósito y les muestra a los niños que dar lo mejor de sí es lo más divertido. La Manada 120 se fundó originalmente con los Ruritanos de Keezletown en Keezletown, Virginia. Durante muchos años, nos acogió la Iglesia Metodista Unida Vision of Hope en Port Republic Road, Rockingham, Virginia. A partir de 2024, nos complace recibir a la Iglesia Presbiteriana Massanutten. Recibimos con agrado a cualquier Scout, pero actualmente nos nutrimos principalmente de las escuelas primarias Cub Run y ​​Peak View del condado de Rockingham, y varios Scouts también provienen de escuelas primarias de Harrisonburg.
Como uno de los grupos de Cub Scouts más grandes y activos del Distrito Mountain Valley del Consejo de Virginia Headwaters, nuestro vibrante grupo de niños y padres involucrados planifican numerosos eventos durante todo el año, proyectos orientados al servicio, junto con viajes divertidos y educativos dentro del Valle de Shenandoah y áreas circundantes.
Normalmente celebramos nuestras reuniones de manada el segundo o tercer lunes de cada mes a las 18:00 h en la Iglesia Presbiteriana Massanutten (50 Indian Trail Rd, Penn Laird, VA 22846). Nuestros Scouts disfrutan del aire libre, así que organizamos tantas actividades al aire libre como podemos.
Uno de los objetivos principales de la Manada 120 es garantizar que los Scouts tengan una experiencia positiva, tengan todas las oportunidades de participar en eventos y disfruten del camino. El Escultismo es lo que los Scouts y sus familias hacen del programa, y ​​seguimos contando con un gran grupo de Scouts y padres que lo hacen posible cada año.

Hello Pack 120 Families With the start of a new scouting year comes one of our important traditions - Popcorn & Peanut fundraising! This effort directly supports Pack activities, helping us funding adventures for every scout.
Our Pack goal is a blend of sales and dues:
Target: $300 in sales per Scout or a combination: $150 sales + $40 dues or higher dues: $80 dues How We Sell Show & Sell (Storefront Sales) - Scouts sell from our inventory at local stores. Take Orders - Scouts take orders from family, friends, neighbors, co-workers, etc., then deliver in November. Show & Sell Dates 9/13 - Rocking R Hardware 9/20 - Lowe's 9/28 - TBD (need a volunteer coordinator for setup/takedown - we're out of town) Additional October dates are likely. We're also exploring Food Lion and welcome other suggestions! Please sign up for 1-hour parent & scout shifts here:
Show & Sell Signup Genius
Daily sales will be split hourly between participating Scouts. We've stocked extra $10 items this year since they sold out quickly in 2024.
Take Orders Order forms will be handed out at the Sept. 15 Pack meeting. Orders with payment due Sunday, Oct. 19 to your Den Leader or me (Mark Kipps). Payments can be made by cash, check, or Venmo (@mkipps). If using Venmo, please email me so I can track it. Online Sales Peanuts are not available online. Popcorn is sold via Pecatonica River Popcorn. Products differ from Take Orders (e.g., combo flavors vs. singles). Invitations will be emailed this week - share them via email or social media! Scouts get full credit for online orders. Selling Tips Think family, friends, neighbors, coworkers, church members, and community connections. Door-to-door sales with a parent or trusted adult are often very successful. Class A uniforms are effective at representing scouting and increasing sales. Resources Attached are:
(PDF) Product brochures for (Pecatonica) Popcorn and (Whitley’s) Peanuts Fundraising FAQ I’ll review the program and answer questions at the Sept. 15 Pack meeting, and distribute hardcopy order forms. Excerpts of products offered for sale are below.
Thank you for your support in making this fundraiser a success! With everyone’s help, we’ll fund a great year of Scouting adventures.
Yours in Scouting,
Mark Kipps
Pack 120 – Treasurer & Popcorn Kernel
